children: Retail sales in the U.K. rebounded in August, helped by online sales and shrugging off a pickup in inflation.
Sales volumes were up 0.5% on month, flipping the 0.5% fall in July. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expected a 0.1% decline.

Nonstore sales--typically online--rebounded in August, while sales in department stores also improved after stock availability issues in July, the ONS said. Some of July's overall decline in retail sales was due to seasonal discounting in June.
However, fuel sales were down in August amid surging prices due to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. Headline inflation climbed to 3.1% in August, from 2.9% in July.

The British consumer has been relatively resilient to the impact of the war so far this year. Sales volumes were up 2.4% compared with the same month of 2025, and consumer confidence has recovered above levels seen before the conflict.
